claim: The authors developed a novel approach in C. elegans that uses single-cell RNA sequencing to map eQTLs at cellular resolution in a single one-pot experiment.
source: We developed a novel approach in the model nematode Caenorhabditis elegans that uses single-cell RNA sequencing to map eQTLs at cellular resolution in a single one-pot experiment.
evidence: The abstract directly states this as a methodological development of the study.

claim: The authors mapped eQTLs across cell types in an extremely large population of genetically distinct C. elegans individuals.
source: We mapped eQTLs across cell types in an extremely large population of genetically distinct C. elegans individuals.
evidence: The abstract states this as a key finding, supported by the experimental design described in the methods.

claim: Cell-type-specific trans eQTL hotspots affect the expression of core pathways in the relevant cell types.
source: We found cell-type-specific trans eQTL hotspots that affect the expression of core pathways in the relevant cell types.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by data presented in Figure 4 and related analyses.

claim: The authors found single-cell-specific eQTL effects in the nervous system, including an eQTL with opposite effects in two individual neurons.
source: Finally, we found single-cell-specific eQTL effects in the nervous system, including an eQTL with opposite effects in two individual neurons.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by data in Figure 5C and 5D showing opposing effects in RIM and RIC neurons.

claim: eQTL effects can be specific down to the level of single cells.
source: Our results show that eQTL effects can be specific down to the level of single cells.
evidence: This conclusion is stated in the abstract and supported by the single-neuron eQTL data presented in the results.

claim: Thousands of regions affecting gene expression, termed expression quantitative trait loci (eQTLs), have been identified through genome-wide studies.
source: Gene expression differences have a strong genetic basis, and genome-wide studies have identified thousands of regions affecting gene expression, termed expression quantitative trait loci (eQTLs) (Albert and Kruglyak, 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: eQTLs have been found to underlie genetic associations with complex traits and diseases.
source: eQTLs have been found to underlie genetic associations with complex traits and diseases (Albert and Kruglyak, 2015; Gusev et al., 2014; Hormozdiari et al., 2018)
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: Many eQTLs are cell-type specific.
source: Studies in purified blood cell populations (Raj et al., 2014; Fairfax et al., 2012; Ishigaki et al., 2017) and computational analyses in human tissues (Donovan et al., 2020; Kim-Hellmuth et al., 2020) indicate that many eQTLs are cell-type specific.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple previous studies.

claim: Studying eQTLs in relevant tissues and cell types is important for understanding their role in trait variation.
source: Studying eQTLs in relevant tissues and cell types is thus important for understanding their role in trait variation (Yao et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Studying multiple tissues or cell types is laborious and expensive, and has mostly been limited to large consortia.
source: First, studying multiple tissues or cell types is laborious and expensive, and has mostly been limited to large consortia (GTEx Consortium, 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation and represents established knowledge in the field.

claim: Diseases can be associated with specific subsets of cells that may not be readily separable from the rest of the tissue.
source: Additionally, diseases can be associated with specific subsets of cells that may not be readily separable from the rest of the tissue, limiting the insight that can be gleaned from studying bulk tissue samples (van der Wijst et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Single-cell RNA sequencing has the potential to significantly mitigate challenges in cell-type-specific eQTL mapping.
source: The recently developed technology of single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) has the potential to significantly mitigate both of the above issues.
evidence: This is an inference based on the capabilities of scRNA-seq technology described in the text.

claim: In scRNA-seq, gene expression is profiled at the level of individual cells, and different cell populations are identified based on their gene expression profiles.
source: In scRNA-seq, gene expression is profiled at the level of individual cells, and different cell populations are identified based on their gene expression profiles.
evidence: This describes the basic principle of scRNA-seq technology, which is established knowledge.

claim: scRNA-seq allows simultaneous measurement of expression in multiple tissues and cell types in a 'one-pot' experiment.
source: This approach allows simultaneous measurement of expression in multiple tissues and cell types in a 'one-pot' experiment, reducing the number of samples that need to be processed and profiled separately.
evidence: This describes a key advantage of the scRNA-seq approach as applied in this study.

claim: The size and complexity of mammalian tissues has limited the ability to use scRNA-seq for eQTL mapping.
source: The size and complexity of mammalian tissues has so far limited the ability to use scRNA-seq for eQTL mapping, and studies have focused on purified cell populations and cell lines (Cuomo et al., 2020; van der Wijst et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies and describes the state of the field.

claim: C. elegans has an invariant cell lineage that leads to each individual having the same number and identity of cells.
source: One of the mainstays of modern genetic research, C. elegans has an invariant cell lineage that leads to each individual having the same number and identity of cells (Sulston and Horvitz, 1977).
evidence: This is a well-established fact about C. elegans biology, supported by a citation.

claim: Decades of research have uncovered the functions of many C. elegans cells, as well as expression markers that uniquely identify them.
source: Decades of research have uncovered the functions of many of those cells, as well as expression markers that uniquely identify them (Hall and Altun, 2007; Hobert et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work and represents established knowledge.

claim: C. elegans is exceptionally well-suited for using scRNA-seq to map eQTLs across cell types in the natural physiological context of a whole animal, down to cellular resolution.
source: These features and resources make C. elegans exceptionally well-suited for using scRNA-seq to map eQTLs across cell types in the natural physiological context of a whole animal, down to cellular resolution.
evidence: This is an inference based on the described features of C. elegans and the capabilities of scRNA-seq.

claim: The authors recently developed a method called C. elegans extreme quantitative trait locus (ceX-QTL) mapping for genetic analysis of complex traits in extremely large populations of segregants.
source: We recently developed a method, C. elegans extreme quantitative trait locus (ceX-QTL) mapping, for genetic analysis of complex traits in extremely large populations of segregants (Burga et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: The ceX-QTL method takes advantage of a mutation in the gene fog-2 that forces the normally hermaphroditic C. elegans to reproduce via obligate outcrossing.
source: The method takes advantage of a mutation in the gene fog-2 that forces the normally hermaphroditic C. elegans to reproduce via obligate outcrossing, allowing us to propagate a large crossing experiment for multiple generations.
evidence: This describes a key feature of the ceX-QTL method, supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The authors propagated a cross between the laboratory strain N2 and a highly divergent isolate from Hawaii, CB4856, for four generations, generating a pool of 200,000 genetically distinct F4 segregants.
source: We propagated a cross between the laboratory strain N2 and a highly divergent isolate from Hawaii, CB4856, for four generations, generating a pool of 200,000 genetically distinct F4 segregants.
evidence: This describes the experimental design and is supported by the methods section.

claim: The authors dissociated the segregant pool to single cells at the L2 larval stage and profiled the cells with scRNA-seq.
source: We dissociated the segregant pool to single cells at the L2 larval stage and profiled the cells with scRNA-seq.
evidence: This describes the experimental procedure.

claim: The final dataset comprises 55,508 cells classified into 19 different cell types.
source: Our final dataset comprises 55,508 cells classified into 19 different cell types (Figure 1B; Supplementary file 1—Table S1).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the dataset composition, supported by Figure 1B.

claim: The observed number of cells of each type was strongly correlated with the known cell-type abundance in L2 larvae (Spearman's ρ=0.87, p=2.2×10−6).
source: The observed number of cells of each type was strongly correlated with the known cell-type abundance in L2 larvae (Spearman's ρ=0.87, p=2.2×10−6, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This statistical result is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Most of the cells in the sample were expected to carry unique genotypes.
source: Most of the cells in our sample were expected to carry unique genotypes (Materials and methods, Supplementary file 1—Table S1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by calculations in the methods section.

claim: The design of having unique genotypes is advantageous for eQTL mapping because it maximizes the sample size.
source: This design is advantageous for eQTL mapping because it maximizes the sample size (Mandric et al., 2020)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Transcriptomic data can be used for genotyping by leveraging variants in transcribed sequences.
source: Previous studies have shown that in addition to providing a readout of global gene expression, transcriptomic data can also be used for genotyping by leveraging variants in transcribed sequences (Ronald et al., 2005; West et al., 2006; Kang et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The authors built a hidden Markov model (HMM) for genotyping cells based on scRNA-seq data.
source: To that end, we built a HMM for genotyping cells based on scRNA-seq data.
evidence: This describes a methodological development of the study.

claim: The HMM calculates the posterior probability of the underlying genotypes for each individual based on three components: prior probabilities, emission probabilities, and transition probabilities.
source: The model calculates the posterior probability of the underlying genotypes for each individual based on three components: (1) prior probabilities for each of the possible genotypes, (2) emission probabilities for observing variant-informative reads given each of the possible genotypes, and (3) transition probabilities for recombination events occurring or not occurring between adjacent genotype-informative sites.
evidence: This describes the structure of the HMM model developed in the study.

claim: The authors mapped 1718 cis eQTLs in 1294 genes and 451 trans eQTLs in 390 genes at a false discovery rate (FDR) of 10% across the different cell types.
source: We mapped 1718 cis eQTLs in 1294 genes and 451 trans eQTLs in 390 genes at a false discovery rate (FDR) of 10% across the different cell types (Figure 3A, B, Supplementary file 1—Table S2).
evidence: This is a key finding of the study, supported by data shown in Figure 3.

claim: The number of eQTLs detected in each cell type was strongly correlated with the number of cells of that type (Spearman's ρ=0.91, p<2.2×10−16).
source: The number of eQTLs detected in each cell type was strongly correlated with the number of cells of that type (Spearman's ρ=0.91, p<2.2×10−16).
evidence: This statistical result is stated in the text.

claim: In cell types with >1000 cells, the authors mapped between 52 and 415 eQTLs.
source: In cell types with >1000 cells, we mapped between 52 and 415 eQTLs (Supplementary file 1—Table S1).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results.

claim: For 1071 of the 1294 genes with a cis eQTL (83%), the eQTL was detected in only one cell type.
source: For 1071 of the 1294 genes with a cis eQTL (83%), the eQTL was detected in only one cell type.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results.

claim: For 208 of the remaining 223 genes (93%), the direction of the eQTL effect was the same in all cell types in which it was detected.
source: For 208 of the remaining 223 genes (93%), the direction of the eQTL effect was the same in all cell types in which it was detected.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results.

claim: The overlap between single-cell cis eQTLs and those previously identified in a panel of 200 recombinant inbred lines was highly significant, with 335 cis eQTLs shared between the studies (OR = 7.2, p<2.2×10−16).
source: Despite major differences in experimental design, including the developmental stage of the worms, the overlap with the single-cell cis eQTLs was highly significant, with 335 cis eQTLs shared between the studies (OR = 7.2, p<2.2×10−16, Fisher's exact test) (Figure 3C).
evidence: This statistical result is stated in the text and supported by Figure 3C.

claim: The bulk and single-cell eQTL effect sizes were highly correlated (Spearman's ρ=0.64, p<2.2×10−16).
source: Furthermore, the bulk and single-cell eQTL effect sizes were highly correlated (Spearman's ρ=0.64, p<2.2×10−16) (Figure 3D).
evidence: This statistical result is stated in the text and supported by Figure 3D.

claim: Single-cell eQTLs detected in multiple cell types were more likely to also be seen in the bulk study: 50% of the genes with cis eQTLs detected in multiple cell types were also identified in bulk compared to 28% of the eQTLs detected in only one cell type (OR = 2.58, p=2.1×10−8).
source: Lastly, single-cell eQTLs detected in multiple cell types were more likely to also be seen in the bulk study: 50% of the genes with cis eQTLs detected in multiple cell types were also identified in bulk compared to 28% of the eQTLs detected in only one cell type (OR = 2.58, p=2.1×10−8) (Figure 3C).
evidence: This statistical result is stated in the text and supported by Figure 3C.

claim: The single-cell eQTL mapping approach improves the power to detect cell-type-specific effects.
source: This observation suggests that the single-cell eQTL mapping approach improves the power to detect cell-type-specific effects.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that multi-cell-type eQTLs are more likely to be detected in bulk studies.

claim: 90 of the 451 trans eQTLs clustered at five hotspots, each containing 12–31 eQTLs.
source: We observed that 90 of the 451 trans eQTLs clustered at five hotspots, each containing 12–31 eQTLs (Figure 4, Supplementary file 1—Table S3).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results, supported by Figure 4.

claim: A hotspot on Chr. I was identified independently in both neurons and seam cells, with the top associated variant (Chr. I:10890182) being the same for both cell types.
source: A hotspot on Chr. I was identified independently in both neurons and seam cells; the top associated variant (Chr. I:10890182) was the same for both cell types (Figure 4A, B).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results, supported by Figure 4A and 4B.

claim: The targets of the hotspot detected in intestinal cells were weakly enriched for genes involved in the innate immune response (FDR-corrected p=0.042).
source: The targets of the hotspot detected in intestinal cells were weakly enriched for genes involved in the innate immune response (FDR-corrected p=0.042), a major role of that tissue (Pukkila-Worley and Ausubel, 2012).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the GO enrichment analysis results.

claim: The innate immune response is a major role of the intestinal tissue in C. elegans.
source: The targets of the hotspot detected in intestinal cells were weakly enriched for genes involved in the innate immune response (FDR-corrected p=0.042), a major role of that tissue (Pukkila-Worley and Ausubel, 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The targets of the hotspot detected in the body wall muscle were enriched for genes associated with myofilament (FDR corrected p=6.4×10−8), actin cytoskeleton (FDR-corrected p=4.2×10−6), and related terms.
source: The targets of the hotspot detected in the body wall muscle were enriched for genes associated with the term myofilament (FDR corrected p=6.4×10−8), actin cytoskeleton (FDR-corrected p=4.2×10−6), and related terms.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the GO enrichment analysis results.

claim: The enrichment in body wall muscle hotspot targets was driven by the genes mup-2, tni-1, tnt-2, mlc-2, mlc-3, lev-11, and act-4.
source: The enrichment was driven by the genes mup-2, tni-1, tnt-2, mlc-2, mlc-3, lev-11, and act-4.
evidence: This is a direct statement of which genes contributed to the enrichment.

claim: mlc-2 and mlc-3 encode a myosin light chain, and act-4 encodes an actin protein.
source: mlc-2 and mlc-3 encode a myosin light chain, and act-4 encodes an actin protein.
evidence: This describes the known functions of these genes.

claim: lev-11 encodes a tropomyosin, and mup-2, tni-1, and tnt-2 encode three of the four proteins in C. elegans that are expressed in the body-wall muscle and form troponin complexes.
source: lev-11 encodes a tropomyosin, and mup-2, tni-1, and tnt-2 encode three of the four proteins in C. elegans that are expressed in the body-wall muscle and form troponin complexes, highly conserved regulators of muscle contraction (Ono and Ono, 2004; Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes the known functions of these genes, supported by a citation.

claim: Troponin complexes are highly conserved regulators of muscle contraction.
source: lev-11 encodes a tropomyosin, and mup-2, tni-1, and tnt-2 encode three of the four proteins in C. elegans that are expressed in the body-wall muscle and form troponin complexes, highly conserved regulators of muscle contraction (Ono and Ono, 2004; Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: The targets of the neuronal hotspot on the right arm of Chr. III were enriched for genes involved in vesicle localization (FDR-corrected p=7.5×10−3).
source: The targets of the neuronal hotspot on the right arm of Chr. III were enriched for genes involved in vesicle localization (FDR-corrected p=7.5×10−3), as well as for BMP receptor binding genes (FDR-corrected p=2.8×10−3).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the GO enrichment analysis results.

claim: The targets of the neuronal hotspot on the right arm of Chr. III were enriched for BMP receptor binding genes (FDR-corrected p=2.8×10−3).
source: The targets of the neuronal hotspot on the right arm of Chr. III were enriched for genes involved in vesicle localization (FDR-corrected p=7.5×10−3), as well as for BMP receptor binding genes (FDR-corrected p=2.8×10−3).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the GO enrichment analysis results.

claim: The BMP receptor binding enrichment was driven by dbl-1 and tig-2, orthologs of human bone morphogenetic protein (BMP) genes BMP5 and BMP8 and ligands of the transforming growth factor beta (TGF-β) pathway.
source: The latter enrichment was driven by dbl-1 and tig-2, orthologs of human bone morphogenetic protein (BMP) genes BMP5 and BMP8 and ligands of the transforming growth factor beta (TGF-β) pathway (Gumienny, 2013).
evidence: This describes the genes contributing to the enrichment and their known functions, supported by a citation.

claim: dbl-1 was discovered as a gene that regulates body size in C. elegans.
source: Notably, dbl-1 was discovered as a gene that regulates body size in C. elegans (Suzuki et al., 1999)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: The hotspot peak marker is located <300 kb from the peak of a QTL previously identified for body size, and the corresponding confidence intervals overlap.
source: the hotspot peak marker is located <300 kb from the peak of a QTL we previously identified for body size (Andersen et al., 2015), and the corresponding confidence intervals overlap (Supplementary file 1—Table S3)
evidence: This is a direct statement comparing the current results to previous findings.

claim: Differential regulation of the TGF-β pathway is involved in variation in body size between N2 and CB4856.
source: the hotspot peak marker is located <300 kb from the peak of a QTL we previously identified for body size (Andersen et al., 2015), and the corresponding confidence intervals overlap (Supplementary file 1—Table S3), suggesting that differential regulation of the TGF-β pathway is involved in variation in body size between N2 and CB4856.
evidence: This is an inference based on the overlap of the hotspot with a body size QTL and the enrichment of TGF-β pathway genes.

claim: The neurons fell into 81 distinct clusters, ranging from 17 to 872 cells.
source: The neurons fell into 81 distinct clusters, ranging from 17 to 872 cells.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the clustering results.

claim: The authors mapped these neuronal clusters onto 100 (83%) of the 120 neuronal clusters identified in CeNGEN.
source: We mapped these clusters onto 100 (83%) of the 120 neuronal clusters identified in CeNGEN (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the mapping results.

claim: The authors identified CEM neurons, which are male specific and absent from CeNGEN, based on the expression of the marker cwp-1.
source: We also identified CEM neurons, which are male specific and absent from CeNGEN, based on the expression of the marker cwp-1 (Portman and Emmons, 2004).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the identification method, supported by a citation.

claim: The authors mapped a total of 163 sn-eQTLs in 132 genes at an FDR of 10%.
source: We mapped cis eQTLs in each of the single neuronal subtypes (sn-eQTLs) and identified a total of 163 sn-eQTLs in 132 genes at an FDR of 10% (Figure 5A, Supplementary file 1—Table S6).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results.

claim: Of the 163 sn-eQTLs, 117 (88%) were identified in only a single neuronal subtype.
source: Of these, 117 (88%) were identified in only a single neuronal subtype.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results.

claim: Functional annotation of sn-eQTLs identified 25 genes involved in signaling (FDR-corrected p=0.047).
source: Functional annotation of sn-eQTLs identified 25 genes involved in signaling (FDR-corrected p=0.047), including 12 genes involved in G-protein coupled receptor signaling (FDR-corrected p=0.047) and eight genes involved in neuropeptide signaling (FDR-corrected p=9.9×10−3).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the GO enrichment analysis results.

claim: 12 genes involved in G-protein coupled receptor signaling were identified among sn-eQTLs (FDR-corrected p=0.047).
source: Functional annotation of sn-eQTLs identified 25 genes involved in signaling (FDR-corrected p=0.047), including 12 genes involved in G-protein coupled receptor signaling (FDR-corrected p=0.047) and eight genes involved in neuropeptide signaling (FDR-corrected p=9.9×10−3).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the GO enrichment analysis results.

claim: Eight genes involved in neuropeptide signaling were identified among sn-eQTLs (FDR-corrected p=9.9×10−3).
source: Functional annotation of sn-eQTLs identified 25 genes involved in signaling (FDR-corrected p=0.047), including 12 genes involved in G-protein coupled receptor signaling (FDR-corrected p=0.047) and eight genes involved in neuropeptide signaling (FDR-corrected p=9.9×10−3).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the GO enrichment analysis results.

claim: 92 sn-eQTLs were not identified pan-neuronally at an FDR of 10%.
source: We compared the sn-eQTLs to those identified when all neurons were analyzed jointly ('pan-neuronal mapping') and found that a sizable fraction of the sn-eQTLs did not have evidence for a pan-neuronal signal: 92 were not identified pan-neuronally at an FDR of 10% and 69 were not identified even at a highly permissive FDR of 50%, suggesting that they exert their effects only in specific neuronal subtypes (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results.

claim: 69 sn-eQTLs were not identified pan-neuronally even at a highly permissive FDR of 50%.
source: We compared the sn-eQTLs to those identified when all neurons were analyzed jointly ('pan-neuronal mapping') and found that a sizable fraction of the sn-eQTLs did not have evidence for a pan-neuronal signal: 92 were not identified pan-neuronally at an FDR of 10% and 69 were not identified even at a highly permissive FDR of 50%, suggesting that they exert their effects only in specific neuronal subtypes (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results.

claim: Among the 69 sn-eQTLs with no signal in the pan-neuronal mapping even at the permissive FDR, the direction of the effect was concordant for 33 and discordant for 36, not significantly different from chance (p>0.5; binomial test).
source: Among the 69 sn-eQTLs with no signal in the pan-neuronal mapping even at the permissive FDR, the direction of the effect was concordant for 33 and discordant for 36, not significantly different from chance (p>0.5; binomial test), as would be expected if these effects are truly subtype-specific (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the statistical analysis results.

claim: Among the 94 sn-eQTLs that had a pan-neuronal signal at an FDR of 50%, the direction of the effect was concordant for 88 and discordant for only 6 (p<0.000001; binomial test).
source: In contrast, among the 94 that had a pan-neuronal signal at an FDR of 50%, the direction of the effect was concordant for 88 and discordant for only 6 (p<0.000001; binomial test), consistent with differences in detection arising from limited statistical power.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the statistical analysis results.

claim: An sn-eQTL in the neuropeptide gene nlp-21 showed significant and opposing effects in two neurons.
source: In a striking case, we observed an sn-eQTL in the neuropeptide gene nlp-21 that showed significant and opposing effects in two neurons (Figure 5C, D).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results, supported by Figure 5C and 5D.

claim: In the RIC neuron, higher nlp-21 expression was associated with the CB4856 allele (β = 4.4, FDR-corrected p=0.03).
source: In the RIC neuron, higher nlp-21 expression was associated with the CB4856 allele (β = 4.4, FDR-corrected p=0.03)
evidence: This is a direct statement of the statistical analysis results.

claim: In the RIM neuron, higher nlp-21 expression was associated with the N2 allele (β = −5.4, FDR-corrected p=9.8×10−7).
source: while in the RIM neuron, higher nlp-21 expression was associated with the N2 allele (β = −5.4, FDR-corrected p=9.8×10−7).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the statistical analysis results.

claim: In the pan-neuronal mapping, no significant effect is observed for nlp-21.
source: In the pan-neuronal mapping, no significant effect is observed for this gene.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results.

claim: The directions of the nlp-21 expression differences in RIC and RIM neurons in the parental dataset agreed with the eQTL effects.
source: We identified the RIC and RIM neurons in the parental dataset, and although the small number of cells in each group (35 and 27, respectively, with only 9 and 5 of them from CB4856) was insufficient for statistical testing, the directions of the differences agreed with the eQTL effects (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results, supported by Figure 5E.

claim: Earlier scRNA-seq eQTL mapping studies were limited in sample size to at most ~100 individuals.
source: Earlier scRNA-seq eQTL mapping studies were limited in sample size to at most ~100 individuals, but nevertheless highlighted the potential of this approach to identify cell-type (van der Wijst et al., 2018) and developmental (Cuomo et al., 2020) eQTLs, as well as loci affecting expression variance (Sarkar et al., 2019).
evidence: This describes the state of the field based on citations to previous work.

claim: The novel approach allowed the authors to map eQTLs in tens of thousands of genotypically distinct individuals.
source: Our novel approach allowed us to map eQTLs in tens of thousands of genotypically distinct individuals and enabled detection of both cis and trans eQTLs, as well as resolution of their effects down to the level of specific cells.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the capabilities of the approach.

claim: By using scRNA-seq, the authors were able to process all individuals jointly.
source: By using scRNA-seq, we were able to process all individuals jointly.
evidence: This describes a key advantage of the experimental design.

claim: After the initial parental cross, all subsequent steps carried out over the course of five C. elegans life cycles (3 weeks) were performed in bulk.
source: After the initial parental cross, all subsequent steps carried out over the course of five C. elegans life cycles (3 weeks) were performed in bulk, limiting any confounding environmental factors.
evidence: This describes the experimental design.

claim: The authors synchronized the worms at the first larval stage, L1, and collected samples at the L2 stage to minimize the influence of genotype on development.
source: To minimize the influence of genotype on development, we synchronized the worms at the first larval stage, L1, and collected samples at the L2 stage, limiting the time for differences to accumulate post synchronization.
evidence: This describes the experimental design rationale.

claim: Previous work suggested the existence of cell-type-specific eQTL hotspots in C. elegans based on the expression patterns of hotspot targets.
source: Previous work suggested the existence of cell-type-specific eQTL hotspots in C. elegans based on the expression patterns of hotspot targets (Francesconi and Lehner, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The authors discovered three hotspots that are cell-type specific, with targets that are involved in core functions performed by these cell types.
source: We discovered three hotspots that are cell-type specific, with targets that are involved in core functions performed by these cell types.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the findings.

claim: eQTL hotspots have been identified in human blood cells.
source: Recently, eQTL hotspots have been identified in human blood cells (Yao et al., 2017; Kolberg et al., 2020), as well as in cell lines (Brynedal et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Hotspot and trans eQTL discovery is facilitated by expression studies that can distinguish cell types.
source: These results suggest that hotspot and trans eQTL discovery is facilitated by expression studies that can distinguish cell types and point to a larger role of hotspots in the genetics of gene expression in animals.
evidence: This is an inference based on the results of the study and comparison to previous work.

claim: The extent to which eQTL hotspots play a role in determining biological phenotypes is unknown.
source: The extent to which eQTL hotspots play a role in determining biological phenotypes is unknown, although several examples have been described in animals and plants (Albert and Kruglyak, 2015; Brynedal et al., 2017; Pang et al., 2019; Andersen et al., 2014; Orozco et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: One of the neuronal hotspots identified in this study affects the expression of members of the TGF-β pathway, which has been linked to the control of body size in C. elegans.
source: One of the neuronal hotspots we identified in this study affects the expression of members of the TGF-β pathway, which has been linked to the control of body size in C. elegans (Gumienny, 2013).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the findings, supported by a citation.

claim: A previous study mapped a QTL for body size in a cross between N2 and CB4856 to the same region as the neuronal hotspot.
source: Remarkably, our previous study mapped a QTL for body size in a cross between N2 and CB4856 to the same region (Andersen et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: Resolving the physiological impact of eQTL hotspots will require fine-mapping to identify the underlying causal variants.
source: Ultimately, resolving the physiological impact of eQTL hotspots, including the ones in this study, will require fine-mapping to identify the underlying causal variants.
evidence: This is a statement about future research needs.

claim: A systematic approach for fine-mapping eQTL hotspots has recently been developed in yeast.
source: A systematic approach for fine-mapping eQTL hotspots has recently been developed in yeast (Lutz et al., 2019); future advances may enable this to be carried out in animals as well.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: A comparison of the single-cell cis eQTLs to those mapped in a previous whole-worm eQTL study showed a highly significant overlap despite major differences in experimental design.
source: A comparison of the single-cell cis eQTLs to those mapped in a previous whole-worm eQTL study from our laboratory showed a highly significant overlap despite major differences in experimental design.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the findings.

claim: A sizable fraction of cis eQTLs have robust, consistent effects.
source: These results join accumulating evidence that a sizable fraction of cis eQTLs have robust, consistent effects (GTEx Consortium, 2020; Smith and Kruglyak, 2008)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Many of the cis eQTL effects are conserved across worm development.
source: These results join accumulating evidence that a sizable fraction of cis eQTLs have robust, consistent effects (GTEx Consortium, 2020; Smith and Kruglyak, 2008) and show that many of the effects are conserved across worm development.
evidence: This is an inference based on the comparison between L2 and L4 stage data.

claim: The strong overlap of cis eQTLs mapped by scRNA-seq and whole-worm analysis suggests that the effect of many cis eQTLs is conserved across cell types.
source: The strong overlap of cis eQTLs mapped by scRNA-seq and whole-worm analysis also suggests that the effect of many cis eQTLs is conserved across cell types.
evidence: This is an inference based on the comparison between single-cell and bulk data.

claim: Modeling strategies that borrow power among cell types could increase the power to detect eQTLs.
source: This observation suggests that modeling strategies that borrow power among cell types could increase the power to detect eQTLs.
evidence: This is a speculation about future methodological improvements.

claim: The approach for cis eQTL discovery could be supplemented with tests for allele-specific expression (ASE).
source: In addition, our approach for cis eQTL discovery could be supplemented with tests for allele-specific expression (ASE).
evidence: This is a speculation about future methodological improvements.

claim: The increasing throughput of single-cell technologies and sequencing platforms will enable future work to study cell-type specificity of cis and trans eQTLs in greater detail.
source: Thus, the increasing throughput of single-cell technologies and sequencing platforms will enable future work to study cell-type specificity of cis and trans eQTLs in greater detail.
evidence: This is a speculation about future research possibilities.

claim: The authors discovered cis eQTLs that act in single subtypes of C. elegans neurons, including many that were not found when all neurons were analyzed jointly.
source: Lastly, we discovered cis eQTLs that act in single subtypes of C. elegans neurons, including many that were not found when all neurons were analyzed jointly.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the findings.

claim: The authors discovered an eQTL that influences expression of the gene nlp-21 in opposing directions in two different neurons.
source: Importantly, we also discovered an eQTL that influences expression of the gene nlp-21 in opposing directions in two different neurons.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the findings.

claim: Antagonistic eQTL effects could result from context-dependent effects of the same variant or from different variants acting in each cell.
source: Such antagonism could result from context-dependent effects of the same variant or from different variants acting in each cell.
evidence: This is speculation about the mechanisms underlying the observed antagonistic effects.

claim: A growing body of work has identified eQTLs that are specific to cell types.
source: Our study joins a growing body of work that identified eQTLs that are specific to cell types (Fairfax et al., 2012; Ishigaki et al., 2017; Donovan et al., 2020; Kim-Hellmuth et al., 2020; van der Wijst et al., 2018; Zhang et al., 2018; Westra et al., 2015), as well as developmental (Cuomo et al., 2020; Francesconi and Lehner, 2014) and environmental (Orozco et al., 2012; Fairfax and Knight, 2014; Kim-Hellmuth et al., 2017) contexts.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple previous studies.

claim: Distinct genetic effects are found across cell types and conditions.
source: Distinct genetic effects are found across cell types and conditions, and large-scale study of such effects is therefore crucial for gaining a comprehensive understanding of regulatory variation.
evidence: This is a general conclusion based on the study's findings and previous work.

claim: Large-scale study of context-specific genetic effects is crucial for gaining a comprehensive understanding of regulatory variation.
source: Distinct genetic effects are found across cell types and conditions, and large-scale study of such effects is therefore crucial for gaining a comprehensive understanding of regulatory variation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the findings of the study.

claim: The authors found 870 differentially expressed genes between N2 and CB4856 (at a greater than twofold change and FDR of 10%).
source: We found 870 differentially expressed genes (at a greater than twofold change and FDR of 10%), of which 201 (23%) had a cis eQTL in the same tissue (odds ratio [OR] = 18.8, p<2.2×10−16, Fisher's exact test).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the differential expression analysis results.

claim: 201 (23%) of the 870 differentially expressed genes had a cis eQTL in the same tissue (OR = 18.8, p<2.2×10−16).
source: We found 870 differentially expressed genes (at a greater than twofold change and FDR of 10%), of which 201 (23%) had a cis eQTL in the same tissue (odds ratio [OR] = 18.8, p<2.2×10−16, Fisher's exact test).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the statistical analysis results.

claim: 191 of the 201 cis eQTLs (95%) showed the same direction of effect as the parental difference.
source: In total, 191 of these cis eQTL (95%) showed the same direction of effect as the parental difference.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results.

claim: The effect sizes of the significant cis eQTLs were strongly correlated with the sizes of the parental differences (Spearman's ρ=0.66, p<2.2×10−16).
source: Further, the effect sizes of the significant cis eQTLs were strongly correlated with the sizes of the parental differences (Spearman's ρ=0.66, p<2.2×10−16) (Figure 3—figure supplements 1 and 2).
evidence: This statistical result is stated in the text and supported by Figure 3—figure supplements 1 and 2.

claim: For a sizable fraction of the genes with cis eQTLs, those cis eQTLs are a major cause of differential gene expression between the strains.
source: These results provide independent support for our cis eQTL mapping and show that for a sizable fraction of the genes those cis eQTLs are a major cause of differential gene expression between the strains.
evidence: This is an inference based on the concordance between cis eQTLs and parental differences.
